Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Transient stimulus with long-term chromatin accessibility tracking (ATAC-seq time course)
ideas.description: Expose cells to a brief stimulus (e.g., TPA, growth factor, or injury), then profile ATAC-seq and AP-1 (FOS/JUN) CUT&RUN at intervals from hours to weeks after the stimulus is removed. Like patination, a mark left on a stone after the original process ends, persistence of AP-1-dependent open sites after AP-1 binding decays would indicate memory. Compare the sites with those of naive cells.

ideas.title: Acute AP-1 degradation to separate initiation from maintenance
ideas.description: Use a degron (dTAG/AID) on FOS or JUN, or a dominant-negative such as A-FOS, and remove AP-1 at different times after the stimulus: before, during, and long after. If accessibility and the faster re-induction of target genes persist after AP-1 is gone, AP-1 is needed only to write the memory. If they collapse, AP-1 is needed to maintain it.

ideas.title: Re-stimulation challenge: primed vs. naive transcriptional response
ideas.description: Give two pulses of stimulus separated by variable rest intervals and measure nascent RNA (PRO-seq or scRNA-seq) of AP-1 target genes after the second pulse. Memory predicts faster or stronger induction in primed cells, with a decay time that can be fitted to a model. Test whether this priming requires AP-1 by degrading it only during the first pulse.

ideas.title: Single-cell multiome and lineage tracing of memory inheritance through division
ideas.description: Run paired scATAC/scRNA-seq on sister cells after live-imaging AP-1 reporter activity or barcoded lineage tracing. This tests whether AP-1-opened chromatin states are inherited by daughter cells in a clonal pattern, and whether they persist across several divisions without ongoing AP-1 activity. The analysis would compare within-clone and between-clone similarity of chromatin state and response.

ideas.title: Causal sufficiency tests with synthetic AP-1 recruitment and histone-mark profiling
ideas.description: Transiently recruit AP-1 (optogenetic or dCas9-tethered FOS/JUN) to a specific locus or reporter and test whether accessibility, H3K27ac and the response to a later stimulus persist after recruitment ends. Profile cooperating factors and chromatin remodelers (BAF, p300) at the site to see which are needed for persistence. This tests whether AP-1 is sufficient to create a heritable state, not just correlated with one.
